question: A 73-year-old patient presented complete neurological dysphagia in the swallowing test, secondary to a cadioembolic stroke in the territory of the left middle cerebral artery. You will need long-term nutritional support. Of the following treatment modalities, which one do you consider most appropriate for this case?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Neurological dysphagia due to stroke -> difficulty swallowing -> risk of malnutrition -> need for long-term nutritional support -> 80% CHAIN: Left middle cerebral artery territory stroke -> impaired swallowing function -> requirement for alternative feeding methods -> consideration of enteral nutrition -> 75% CHAIN: Complete neurological dysphagia -> inability to swallow safely -> high risk of aspiration -> indication for enteral nutrition -> 70% CHAIN: Cardioembolic stroke -> left middle cerebral artery involvement -> neurological dysphagia -> long-term nutritional support required -> 80%
enhanced_information: For a 73-year-old patient with complete neurological dysphagia post-cardioembolic stroke in the left middle cerebral artery territory requiring long-term nutritional support, enteral nutrition via gastrostomy is the most appropriate treatment modality. This choice is supported by the patient's inability to swallow safely, high risk of aspiration, and the need for alternative feeding methods due to impaired swallowing function.
